notes: Minimum cacheable prefix 1024 tokens for GPT-5.6 and later; varies by model and request settings for earlier models.
Default minimum cache lifetime is 30 minutes; a 12-hour minimum lifetime writes at 2.5x base input (Responses API).
The lifetime is a MINIMUM: OpenAI may retain entries longer, so a hard-expiry simulation is conservative (real hit rates can be higher).
Cache reads 0.1x base input on most GPT-5.6+ models; 0.05x on GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6.1 Terra.
Write rates are totals, not surcharges: each input token is billed at exactly one of uncached / cache-write / cached-read rate.
Models before GPT-5.6 have no cache-write charge (read discount only) and use prompt_cache_retention instead of ttl.
Cached-token reporting rounds down to a multiple of 128 tokens.
The rendered prefix is the cache key: settings such as reasoning.effort, text.verbosity and context_management compaction can change it.
Caching is on by default (implicit); explicit breakpoints available via prompt_cache_options (up to 4 writes per request).

Pre-GPT-5.6 models: docs confirm no cache-write charge, but the cached-input read rate is model-dependent and could not be verified on 2026-10-28 (pricing page is JS-rendered). Savings are NOT estimated for this family until the user supplies verified rates via --rules.
Default cache lifetime 5 minutes, refreshed on each cache read; a 1-hour duration writes at 2x base input.
Cache reads 0.1x base input (per-model exceptions in the source table).
Billing breakdown per request: total input = cache_read + cache_creation + input tokens; tokens after the last breakpoint are always uncached.
Caching requires cache_control breakpoints (explicit or top-level automatic).
Concurrent requests: a cache entry is only available after the first response begins.
For models not in the minimums table, the strictest known minimum (4096, Opus 4.5/4.6) is assumed, so savings are understated rather than overstated.
